page0.text:
Ryudou Temple.
Now a barren place since Caster's demise.
The monks who collapsed due to an unknown illness all left the mountain, leaving the temple completely uninhabited.
The gates are tightly shut to even residents of the temple, to say nothing of visitors.

page1.text:
"Tch. It reeks something awful. No one told me anything about the stench."
A voice echoes in the empty temple grounds.
His lithe blue form is illuminated by the moonlight.
The muscular body without a gram of excess, and the long scarlet weapon belong to the Servant called Lancer.

page2.text:
"Well, well. The Bounded Field's still up even after its owner kicked the bucket.
...No, its repulsiveness has increased by half compared to before. Caster's work was impressive, compared to this."

page3.text:
Lancer casually peers out over the temple grounds.
He grips his crimson spear.
Intelligence-gathering and observation are his primary tasks.
He isn't happy about it, but orders are orders.
It's his policy to follow his lord's commands and deliver the results asked of him.
Accordingly, he's skirmished with several Servants so far and disengaged each time.

page4.text:
Lancer hasn't fought any battles on his own initiative, per his contract with his Master.
Tonight's scouting mission to Ryudou Temple is no exception.
So, he shouldn't need his spear.
He can conjure his Noble Phantasm any time he wishes.
One would think it unnecessary to be armed when there's no enemy to fight.

page5.text: "All this damn chirping. I figured Caster for a wind-user, but maybe she used water, too. This place is crawling with spiders and leeches and so on."

page6.text:
He walks through the temple grounds.
His manner appears utterly defenseless and unbecoming of a Servant.
So unguarded is he that on the off chance another Servant is lurking nearby, he would surely perish in an ambush.

page7.text:
"Yeah I suppose, someone might have switched heads with her.
There's nothing but rotten bugs here. Building a nest in someone's abandoned house is par for the course for you lot."

page8.text:
Lancer's foul mood doesn't lift.
The blue-clad spearman admonishes someone who isn't present.

page9.text:
"There was one big one, though.
I don't know where it's from, but it was living amongst the mountain beasts. Plus, is that...sand I smell?
Ha. Here I was imagining some giant spider, when it was just a filthy sand worm.
Gods be damned, why do I have to track this gloomy bastard!?"

page10.text:
He bats aside a silver flash of light.
With a single flourish of his spear, Lancer deflects three deadly darts from the darkness.

page11.text:
The wicked daggers plunge into the ground.
They are dirks: short knives made not for slicing, but skewering their unlucky target.
Each was hurled with unerring accuracy at Lancer's two eyes and windpipe, respectively.

page12.text:
"Nice throw. But don't bother trying again, sand worm.
It isn't my style to lose my life without even an introduction first. Though, it's yours that's ripe for the taking."

page13.text:
The muscled blue form faces the darkness.
Something faintly shifts in the gloom of the shrine.
A skull laughs, its bony facade as white as the moon.

page14.text:
The battle commences without preamble.
The white skull shrieks in no human tongue as it attacks Lancer,
who meets its ambush without so much as twitching an eyebrow.

page15.text:
The skull's thrown dirks are on par with Archer's arrows.
Thirty in total are loosed from the darkness at very close range.
And Lancer parries every single one effortlessly.

page16.text:
"Hee?"
The skull halts.
That's strange.
No matter how capable a spearman Lancer is, he surely can't have blocked every single one of the skull's daggers, each aimed precisely enough to thread a needle.
Moreover, his opponent wields a polearm.
The dirks were aimed at the spear's blind angles and should have struck his opponent's vital points, so how could Lancer have defeated every last one?

page17.text:
"Hey. Don't tell me that's all there is to your tricks."
Lancer's demeanor changes.
He stops, and his merely curious hostility shifts to a determined intent to kill the skull.

page18.text:
"If so, you're finished.
I don't know who the hell you are...but I can just tear off that mask to find out."

page19.text:
More daggers surge out of the darkness.
Just as Lancer is about to advance on the skull, he's intercepted by a frenzied barrage!

page20.text:
And that too, is thwarted.
With only a subtle movement of his spear, Lancer nullifies attacks he shouldn't even be able to see.

page21.text:
...
The skull mask trembles.
It doesn't speak, but it gulps down its next shriek, staring in disbelief at the enemy coming for its head.
"Hah, heee!"
It aims another dagger for Lancer's throat between a gap in his spear's movements!

page22.text:
"Hee...!"
The skull mask trembles.
As Lancer's spear deflects the daggers, it spins in a neat circle in Lancer's hands, arching up into the attacking skull's jaw.

page23.text:
Defense and riposte.
Both maneuvers executed perfectly simultaneously.
The skull has no way of defending itself in midflight.

page24.text:
The white mask falls.
Lancer doesn't press the attack.
His orders are to merely observe the enemy.
Even if this is a golden opportunity to execute his opponent, he lacks the authority to make that decision.

page25.text: "I told you, fool. Projectiles won't work on me. Blame yourself for ignoring my warning."

page26.text:
Lancer reorients his spear toward his enemy which is hiding its face and calmly watches.
A dark body.
A right arm contained in bandages.
Its face, once concealed by a white skull mask, is now shrouded in darkness and difficult to make out clearly.

page27.text:
No...
It would be closer to call it featureless, lacking obvious protrusions or depressions.

page28.text:
"GeEEe... YoU Saw. MY fAce. LAnCER."
"Oh, I'm going to get a good look. You're a Servant, no doubt. Now I'll figure out where you're from."
"HeH. i sEE. soMEtHiNg bindS YoUr POWEr. No wOnDER. YOu faiL TO kiLL ME."

page29.text:
The Servant retreats, cloaked in shadow.
A dirk is clutched in its hand, its lethal intent towards Lancer undiminished.

page30.text:
"Give it a rest. I just happened to be born this way. Projectiles from an opponent I can see don't work on me. Unless you've got a strong Noble Phantasm up your sleeve, you won't be able to hurt me throwing weapons from that distance."
"! Ah, YOu HAve A bleSSInG thaT WARds OfF ARROWS. hEH, YOu mUST Be A GReAT hERo, UNliKe ME."

page31.text:
Shadows sway.
The dark Servant crouches down low like a spider,
then suddenly flings another dagger while leaping high into the air.

page32.text:
If its high leap can be compared to that of a deer, then one might compare its frantic scurrying to that of a spider, snake, or scorpion.
The Servant flees, hiding its face. The speed of its flight is on par with Lancer.
But Lancer's explosive bursts of agility are without peer.
It would be unthinkable for him to need more than a moment to close in on his prey.

page33.text: "Tch. I went for the throat, but you're a pesky one. You can't have healed, so you must just be insane."

page34.text:
Lancer gives chase, his enemy skating on the wet surface like a water strider.
His pursuit churns and splits the water in contrast with his target's elegant escape, but the water strider has no hope of outrunning him.

page35.text: "...Tsk. Should've crippled his joints if I'd known the pain would drive him into flight. That wouldn't have worked on any of the others, but now I have to clean up this mess."

page36.text:
For a human, the severing of one's limbs or major arteries is a critical injury.
A laceration to the aorta, for instance, would cause catastrophic blood loss, leading to certain death in combat.
But this logic only applies to a conventional battle between mortals.
It is unrealistic to expect a Servant—a mighty Heroic Spirit—to die of exsanguination.

page37.text:
As they are powered not by blood, but magical energy, injuring a major blood vessel would only amount to less effective, secondary means of harm.
It would be a different story if one were to cripple all four limbs, but no Servant is so easily immobilized.
Any time wasted on less lethal, immobilizing wounds could expose the attacker to a lethal riposte.

page38.text:
"...Now I get it. You're using some trick to suppress your pain, but that only tells me you have no way to heal yourself. I'll settle this in the next blow."
Lancer crosses the body of water in a geysering gust.
In two seconds, his prey will be in hand.
In a flash, he moves to cleave the fleeing water strider from the left hip...!
"...!"
Lancer immediately leaps in retreat.

page39.text:
The water's surface jumps.
No, something in it bares its fangs.
Dark, thin tendrils chase Lancer into the air.
It's as if the water itself attacks him.
The spectacle brings to mind ancient horrors lurking in the ocean depths.

page40.text:
"This thing is..."
Lancer has nowhere to run.
He strikes the water with his spear and uses every rune he possesses to inscribe a Bounded Field into the lakebed, but it is easily consumed by his pursuer.

page41.text:
Dark tentacles surround him, eating up his safe haven second by second.
Activated fully in concert, his runes are powerful enough to defend against a greater Noble Phantasm, but they barely even manage to slow the thing down.
Assassin cackles.
"wHat's WRoNg, lANCEr? It'Ll DevOur yoU uNless YOU MoVE."
The water strider floats on the water, reveling in the sight.

page42.text:
But it too is no exception from the tentacles' hunger.
It doesn't dare approach the blackened water for fear of being consumed.
It knows that the dark tentacles will instantly shift its attention to any new prey.

page43.text: "BUT ThAT won'T Do. I MUsT BE The onE to kIlL YoU. I STiLL laCK eXPErience. Once I TAKE your Life, I wiLL gAIN THE KNOWlEdGe I lack."

page44.text:
Light glints off the strider's dagger.
It throws its dagger at the immobilized Lancer.
Still, it is futile.
Even while fully engaged with his bizarre foe, Lancer is immune to the projectile attack.

page45.text:
"You still don't learn. I can see why you're so eager, though."
Lancer observes the tentacles surrounding him.
Assassin has lured him a considerable distance from shore. It's thirty meters to the nearest bank.
He can easily cross that piddling distance in a single bound...!

page46.text:
"as soOn aS yoU stopPED mOVINg. yoU LosT. i've waTchED Long EnoUGH. tImE to wrAP this UP."
Lancer's body sinks, his spear warping.
He takes a great leap into the air with the aid of his spear.
But then...
"What?"
An utterly simple, straightforward attack is unleashed.

page47.text:
A false heart emerges from Lancer's chest.
From an impossible distance, still bobbing on the lake surface,
Assassin gouges out the spearman's chest.

page48.text:
It is one of the purest forms of magecraft, the most simplified of curses.
A cursed arm specialized in cursing humans, passed down through Middle Eastern magecraft.
Assassin's Noble Phantasm: Zabaniya. Delusional Heartbeat.
It destroys Lancer's heart without fail. The spearman's lifeless body sinks into the dark water.

page49.text:
The water dances.
It writhes in stimulation; restless, brutal, vulgar.
The sight of a caged and starved beast thrown fresh meat would pale before this savagery.
Countless dark tentacle-like appendages consume the man-shaped Heroic Spirit.
Floating on the black lake, the faceless Servant drinks something red in delight.
